title.narrative: Supporting Uganda's Response to TB - Uganda (01-Jan-2024-31-Dec-2026)

description.narrative: Uganda, Tuberculosis, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development of the Republic of Uganda (MoFPED)This program has the following goals: To reduce TB incidence by 20/100,000 from 199 in 2022 to 179/100,000 population by 2026. The objectives of this program are: To increase TB preventive treatment (TPT) coverage among eligible people to > 90% by 2026. To increase TB treatment coverage from 91% in 2022 to 95% by 2026. To increase TB treatment success from 90% in 2022 to 95% by 2026. To increase MDR-TB treatment coverage increased from 36% to 80% by 2026. To increase the proportion of notified new and relapse TB patients diagnosed using WHO recommended rapid tests from 45% to 90% by 2026. To increase Treatment success rate for the TB/HIV co-infected to >90% in 2026. To educe Stigma and discrimination among TB patients from 53.7% to <10% by 2026,. To increase contribution of the private sector to TB case notification from 20% to 35% by 2024/25. To build effective and efficient systems that ensure quality, equitable and timely services. Improve infrastructure for storage, quantify and improve ratiionale use of medicines. To strengthen Laboratory systems. Strengthen Community Health Systems, human rights and Gender responsiveness and ressources

title.narrative: Coverage / Output indicators targets and results for UGA-T-MoFPEDP06
Treatment success rate of RR-TB and/or MDR-TB: Percentage of patients with RR and/or MDR-TB successfully treated
Number of people with TB (all forms) notified among key affected populations/high risk groups (other than prisoners); *includes only those with new and relapse
Number of people in contact with TB patients who began preventive therapy
TBDT- Other 1: Number of Males patients with of all forms of TB notified (i.e., bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed); *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Number of patients with of all forms of TB notified (i.e., bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed); *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Number of people with confirmed RR-TB and/or MDR-TB notified
TBDT- Other 2: Number of <15 years patients with of all forms of TB notified (i.e., bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed); *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Number of people with TB (all forms) notified among prisoners; *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Percentage of TB patients with DST result for at least Rifampicin among the total number of notified (new and retreatment) patients during the reporting period
Percentage of new and relapse TB patients tested using WHO recommended rapid diagnostic tests at the time of diagnosis
Percentage of laboratories successfully participating in external quality assurance (EQA) or proficiency testing (PT) schemes
Percentage of people with confirmed RR-TB and/or MDR-TB that began second-line treatment
Contact investigation coverage: Proportion of contacts of people with bacteriologically confirmed TB evaluated for TB among those eligible

Treatment success rate- all forms: Percentage of patients with all forms of TB, bacteriologically confirmed plus clinically diagnosed, successfully treated (cured plus treatment completed) among all TB patients notified during a specified period; *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Timeliness of reporting: Percentage of submitted monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are received on time per the national guidelines
LMIS Reporting Rate - Percentage of all health facilities that are required to report that submit an LMIS report to central authority
Percentage of HIV-positive new and relapse TB patients on ART during TB treatment
Percentage of registered new and relapse TB patients with documented HIV status
